chapter: Properties of matter: elasticity, viscosity, surface tension

variants.title: Statical torsion: rigidity modulus of a steel rod
variants.method: Statical (Barton's) torsion with a couple from two cords
variants.unknown: the modulus of rigidity of steel
variants.note: Steel is the stiffest of these rods: the same couple twists it least.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, elastic constants of metals (shear modulus of steel 79.3 GPa)

variants.title: Statical torsion: rigidity modulus of a brass rod
variants.method: Statical (Barton's) torsion with a couple from two cords
variants.unknown: the modulus of rigidity of brass
variants.note: Brass has less than half the rigidity of steel, so the pointer swings about twice as far.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, elastic constants of metals (shear modulus of brass 36.5 GPa)

variants.title: Statical torsion: rigidity modulus of a copper rod
variants.method: Statical (Barton's) torsion with a couple from two cords
variants.unknown: the modulus of rigidity of copper
variants.note: Copper sits between brass and steel; it is soft, so unload it and check the pointer returns to zero.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, elastic constants of metals (shear modulus of copper 44.7 GPa)

variants.title: Statical torsion: rigidity modulus of an aluminium rod
variants.method: Statical (Barton's) torsion with a couple from two cords
variants.unknown: the modulus of rigidity of aluminium
variants.note: The softest rod of the set: the twist is large and easy to read, but the elastic limit is close.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, elastic constants of metals (shear modulus of aluminium 26.0 GPa)
